hardware.name: Mac Studio M5 Ultra · 256 GB (36C CPU / 80C GPU)
hardware.usableNote: oMLX allowed ~200.4 GB for a model on the 256 GB unit (MacStories)
hardware.wattsNote: ~214 W peak sustained during LLM inference (256 GB config)
hardware.notes: Quiet desktop; holds 125B-class MoE (Flash-Next 4/5-bit) in memory; RTX 5090 still ~25% faster at decode on models that fit in 32 GB (MacStories).

hardware.name: Mac Studio M5 Ultra · 96 GB (30C CPU / 64C GPU)
hardware.usableNote: Usable share assumed ~78% by analogy with the 256 GB unit's 200/256 (estimate)
hardware.bandwidthNote: Unknown for the 64-core-GPU bin (1.2 TB/s is quoted for M5 Ultra generally)
hardware.notes: Entry Ultra. Fits 27B dense at 8-bit or ~120B MoE at 4-bit with modest context.

hardware.name: Mac Studio M5 Max · 128 GB
hardware.bandwidthNote: per-M5-Max-die figure quoted in r/LocalLLaMA launch thread
hardware.notes: Half the bandwidth of the Ultra. Sunk Cost estimates ~25 tok/s on Qwen3.8 27B Q4 (estimate, not measured).

hardware.name: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) · 128 GB
hardware.priceNote: Founders Edition after Feb 2026 increase from $3,999; 64 GB partner units ship Oct 23, 2026, price not announced
hardware.wattsNote: ~160 W at the wall under GPU-heavy load (240 W PSU)
hardware.notes: Slow single-stream on dense models (~273 GB/s) but excellent batched throughput: gpt-oss-120b 61 → 2,621 tok/s aggregate at 128 concurrent (Certant). Also sold as ASUS GX10.

hardware.name: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo) mini PC · 128 GB
hardware.usableNote: up to 96 GB of the 128 GB can be assigned to graphics
hardware.priceNote: Bosgame M5 $3,324; Framework $3,449 (often unavailable); GMKtec EVO-X2 $3,499.99; Minisforum $3,799; Beelink $4,349; AMD Halo dev box $3,999
hardware.notes: Cheapest way to hold 120B-class MoE in one box. Dense 70B is slow (~4.8 tok/s). Prefill is weak vs discrete GPUs.

hardware.name: GeForce RTX 5090 · 32 GB (card only)
hardware.priceNote: MSRP $1,999, but Sept 2026 street $4,299–$5,300 (GDDR7 shortage). Host PC not included (not priced).
hardware.wattsNote: peak power 567–577 W measured in MacStories' subagent test (PC)
hardware.notes: Fastest single card for models ≤32 GB (Qwen3.8 27B 59 tok/s, 3,031 tok/s prefill). Spills to system RAM beyond that (4.6 tok/s).

hardware.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell · 96 GB (card only)
hardware.priceNote: NVIDIA US price $16,000 (launched ~$8,565); ~$18,000 at Newegg/Amazon Oct 4. Host workstation not included.
hardware.notes: ECC, 96 GB at 5090-class bandwidth. gpt-oss-120b 163 tok/s; Flash-Next NVFP4 ~100 tok/s at 32K.

hardware.name: Used RTX 3090 · 24 GB (card only)
hardware.notes: Budget 24 GB. 3× 3090 ran gpt-oss-120b at 124 tok/s (AIMultiple, Apr 2026) but needs a multi-GPU host.

hardware.name: Used RTX 4090 · 24 GB (card only)
hardware.notes: Same 24 GB as a 3090 for far more money; no 2026 tok/s for current models found → unknown.

quotes.text: GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Next Flash, and even Qwen 3.8 27B are all outperforming (in both intelligence and capabilities) every model that was considered "frontier intelligence" in Xmas 2025.
You don't pick an inference engine first. You pick a hardware strategy, a workload shape, and a serving model. The engine follows.
The personal assistants I use the most are now entirely powered by a model running locally on a Mac Studio.

I use Bonsai for sensitive tasks. Still, I don't use local models for much of my daily routine. They aren't smart enough for what I need, and the open models that are actually capable require heavy-duty hardware I don't have.
By the time you've repaid your investment, you could have used the most expensive Anthropic subscription for several years, still saved money, and got better performance in return.
